**Added: Cloud-gateway reverse registration (R-20261122-004, independent implementation per F-R1-49)** — Internal SSH hosts (no public IP, outbound-only) can now reach the cloud gateway through a reverse Agent tunnel. (1) easyssh-gateway adds agent.rs with the agent-wire/1 framing (DIAL/OPEN_OK/OPEN_ERR/DATA/CLOSE/PING/PONG; binary header [type:1][session_id:8 BE][len:4 BE], heartbeat 30s×3 dead-peer detection) plus GET /agent/connect (separate AgentToken roles=agent auth) and an agent branch in tunnel.rs that reuses the existing forward pumps unchanged. (2) New easyssh-agent crate: Windows service (SCM) and Linux systemd unit, --enroll exchanges an AgentToken (DPAPI / 0600 storage), exponential-backoff reconnect (1s→30s cap), DIAL restricted to the configured local_backend (default 127.0.0.1:22). (3) Full self-service resource workflow: users.db resources table bootstrap, issue.php register/update/delete_resource + upgraded my_resources (direct public probing with SSH-2.0 banner check + SSRF allowlist; agent one-time enrollment token, 10 minutes), gw-admin resource management card, admin user-resource management, gateway /admin/resource with a persisted dynamic registry (resources.dyn.toml), 3 resources per user, POST /agent/enroll. (4) The existing register→email verify→auto-approve→issue chain is unchanged and the client is unaffected. Gates: easyssh-gateway 100/100, easyssh-agent 33/33.

**Added: Macro sequences (R-20261117-004)** — A new "Macros" manager in the toolbar: save multi-step command sequences as reusable macros. Each step can have a pre-execution delay and an optional "wait until output matches regex" condition before the next step runs (Expect-style automation, e.g. wait for a prompt or a service-ready line). Steps can be added, removed, and reordered. At run time steps are sent sequentially to the active session with live progress in the status bar ("Macro running: name (step i/N)") and a one-click stop; wait timeouts and disconnects abort with a clear reason. Macros are stored locally (localStorage) and no macros ship pre-installed.

**Added: Config backup/restore packages + WebDAV cloud sync (R-20261117-005)** — Settings gains a "Backup & Sync" group: (1) pack sessions + known hosts into a single encrypted .esshbak file (passphrase hardened via Argon2id + AES-256-GCM, minimum 8 characters enforced); (2) imports run a preflight report first (new/conflicting sessions, up to 50 listed) and offer merge (keeps existing entries, never overwrites) or replace (double confirmation), with a rolling backup of config.json before any write; (3) optional WebDAV cloud sync (test connection / upload backup / restore), compatible with services like Jianguoyun — local-first with bring-your-own cloud. Key files are DPAPI-bound to this machine and are excluded from packages (stated in the package comment block).

**Added: Broadcast input for multiple sessions (R-20261117-001)** — A new "Broadcast" toolbar toggle (Ctrl+Shift+B): once enabled, every keystroke you type in any terminal (including Enter to execute) is mirrored in real time to all other connected sessions across all tabs, closing the gap with Xshell/MobaXterm-style cluster operations. Safety design: a risk-confirmation dialog appears when enabling with ≥2 sessions (with a dangerous-command warning); disconnected sessions are skipped automatically and rejoin after reconnect; while broadcasting, all panes show a warning border and the status bar shows the live session count; the toggle is not persisted — every launch starts with it off.

**Added: Direct import of PuTTY .ppk private keys (R-20261117-002)** — Users migrating from PuTTY often only have a .ppk key, which previously required a manual PuTTYgen conversion. Selecting a .ppk path in the connect form now converts it automatically before connecting, and an "Import PuTTY .ppk" button (in the key tools area) converts a picked file and fills the private-key path automatically. Supports PPK v2/v3 with ssh-ed25519 / ssh-rsa / ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 and full MAC integrity verification (v2 = HMAC-SHA1, v3 = HMAC-SHA256); passphrase-encrypted .ppk files are not decrypted and produce a clear hint to remove the passphrase in PuTTY first. Converted keys are written as PKCS#8 PEM to keys/imported_*.pem with the public key generated alongside.

**Added: ProxyJump jump-chain diagnostics (R-20261117-003)** — When a jump-chain connection fails, the error now carries "hop N/M (host:port)" pinpointing plus targeted advice for four failure classes (TCP unreachable → check IP/port/firewall; handshake failure → confirm it is an SSH service; authentication failure → check the saved credentials of that hop's session; channel denied → check sshd AllowTcpForwarding). Jump chains longer than 3 hops are now rejected explicitly before connecting (previously silently truncated), with a hint to merge hops or use a proxy; error wording for direct (no-jump) connections is unchanged.

**Website: new Migration Guide (migrating from Xshell / PuTTY / Termius / OpenSSH config, .ppk conversion walkthrough, ProxyJump examples) and Product Comparison pages (vs Xshell / FinalShell / Tabby), in both Chinese and English.**

**Added: download-channel source attribution (attribution phase 2)** — the online update-check response may now carry an officially issued random download token (containing no personal information). The app persists it and attaches it to anonymous statistics reports, building a weak link between an anonymous website visit and anonymous usage statistics to help improve download channels. The token is carried for the lifetime of the device (re-attributed automatically after a clean reinstall) and is covered by the existing statistics privacy switch; older versions behave exactly as before.

**Added: release rollback mechanism** — the website release pipeline now snapshots the pre-release state before touching anything, so an accidental release can be rolled back to the previous version with a single command (see RELEASE.md, section 5).

**Fixed: interface language setting not remembered after restart (R-20261114-004)** — after choosing English/Traditional Chinese/한국어 in Settings and saving, restarting the app reverted to Chinese. The saved language is now applied immediately when settings load at startup.

**Fixed: switching back to Chinese from the English UI did not take effect (R-20261114-003)** — i18n original-text restoration flaw: nodes already translated to English contain no Chinese characters, so the zh-CN restore branch was skipped by the leading CJK regex guard and the original-text backups were never restored. The restore branch now runs first; round-trip switching between Simplified/Traditional/English/Korean applies instantly.

**Improved: UI translations greatly expanded (R-20261114-005)** — the four-language dictionary (Simplified/Traditional/English/Korean) gained 439 entries per language: the toolbar (Quick Commands / Port Forwarding / Split / Feedback / Settings), default quick-command labels (System Info / Disk Usage / Memory / Load & Uptime / Listening Ports / Top Processes / TOP Monitor / Recent Logins / Network Check / Restart sshd / Clear Screen — untouched default commands display translated names), all nine settings groups with their panel labels and descriptions, the master-password / feedback / SFTP / port-forwarding / quick-command dialogs, the command palette, status-bar messages, and more. User-defined commands and session data are never translated.

**Added: Double-click a saved connection entry to connect directly (R-20261113-002)** — Double-clicking a connection record in the session list now starts the connect-server action directly (excluding the delete button). The session is auto-filled back into the form and the existing connection submit flow is triggered natively, fully reusing the entire chain of master password unlock verification / known host fingerprint confirmation / per-session port forwarding auto-start / session saving on success / failure diagnostics, behaving exactly like clicking the "Connect" button; the existing single-click form-fill interaction is unchanged

**Added: Startup fallback guidance when WebView2 Runtime is missing (R-20261112-001)** — On systems that do not ship WebView2 Runtime (e.g. Windows Server 2016/2019), the earliest startup phase (before the WebView is created) checks the official Microsoft registry detection points (EdgeUpdate\Clients under HKLM WOW6432Node/HKLM/HKCU). If missing, a native authorization dialog appears (with two options explained: automatic install / manual install); on agreement, the official Microsoft Evergreen Bootstrapper is downloaded automatically and installed silently with elevation, then re-checked by polling (≤2 minutes) before startup continues; on refusal the app exits after an explanation, and a failed install can be retried. Dialog/ShellExecute use self-declared Win32 FFI, detection uses winreg, download reuses ureq, and it is a no-op on non-Windows

**Improved: Corrected the stats-report debounce status note (R-20261113-001)** — The debounce status file in stats.rs is actually stored in the config directory (not next to the exe); the comment was fixed. This lands alongside the website's stats backend "recent commits" feed and device-activity view released the same day (repeated submissions from the same device after 24h are visible as separate records in the backend; already deployed independently on the website)

**Security: Preparation for update-channel key rotation (R-20261111-001 Phase B)** — The client's online update now supports **dual-key probing**: when decrypting the detection envelope, the new master key is tried first and it automatically falls back to the old key on failure (via the transitional masterPrevBase64 field); download decryption uses the same key that successfully matched the envelope. This prepares the master-key switch of the server-side update channel (encrypted envelopes for update/check) so that both old and new clients can detect updates normally during the switch window. Keys come from update-keys.json in the exe directory (preferred) or build-time embedded config, so rotation requires no code changes (after the transition window, removing the masterPrevBase64 field disables the fallback)

**Security: Website feedback/stats channel master key rotation completed (Phase A, 2026-11-12)** — The server's keys.php master key has been replaced; the old key is kept as master_prev in a dual-key compatibility window (reports from both old and new clients work), to be removed after the window ends

**Added: IP geolocation with primary/backup providers (session context menu "Query server location")** — The primary endpoint is ip.263.tw's encrypted geolocation API (AES-256-GCM payload + /decrypt endpoint, Bearer token auth, 3-second timeout); on failure it automatically falls back to backup ① Baidu (IPv4 only) → backup ② ip-api.com (Chinese-language results, IPv4+IPv6). **Fully IPv6-compatible end to end**: both the primary and backup ② support v6 lookups, avoiding silent failures in v6 scenarios. Reserved/private addresses are never queried externally nor cached (loopback/private/link-local return a classified result directly); normal results are cached locally for 7 days keyed by IP prefix (first two IPv4 octets / first two IPv6 hextets, capped at 512 entries to prevent unbounded growth); when both providers fail it silently degrades without showing an error. The API token is injected via "Settings → geoToken" or the `EASYSSH_GEO_TOKEN` environment variable; bring-your-own is supported, nothing is hardcoded and nothing is stored in the database

**Improved: Stats reporting now works on IPv6-only networks** — On devices with only an IPv6 egress (some mobile networks / campus networks), the "region" field previously came up empty; now fetch_public_ip picks up the public IPv6 and reports it truncated to the first two hextets (e.g. 2408:8207, matching the server's /32 masking form), staying de-identified and never reporting the full IPv6 address

**Improved: Device unique ID extended to 32 hex digits** — The anon_id digest grew from 16 to 32 hex digits (first 16 bytes of SHA-256), reducing collision probability to 2^-128; the website backend's "device unique ID" shows it in full. It remains a one-way hash and cannot be reversed. Note: because the ID changes, old devices will register a new record in the backend, and old records need manual cleanup

**Added: Anonymous client usage statistics (on by default, can be turned off anytime)** — To improve the software, an anonymous stats report is sent once in the background on the first launch of each day: OS version, CPU/memory/disk capacity tiers, software version, system language, and region derived from the first two segments of the public IP. The device identifier is a SHA-256 de-identified anonymous ID and **contains no hostname, MAC address, private IP, full public IP, or any other identity information**; it is transmitted over an encrypted channel (AES-256-GCM + HMAC time-limited signature, same protocol family as online update/feedback). **The collected information is used for statistics only, for no other purpose, and is never shared with any third party.** You can uncheck "Settings → Update → Privacy" to opt out; once off, no reports are sent. This complies with the data-minimization and explicit-notice requirements of the Personal Information Protection Law

**Added: Unified website admin console (easyssh.cn/admin.html)** — Feedback management (migrated from feedback-admin.html; the original address now redirects automatically) and the client stats dashboard are merged into one entry point with one login. The stats dashboard shows cumulative device count / 7-day active / version distribution / OS distribution / CPU·memory·disk tier distribution / language and region distribution / 30-day activity trend. Backend APIs reuse admin-token auth (daily HMAC time-limited token + password hash storage); the stats-report API additionally has per-IP rate limiting, a field whitelist, and a 12-hour per-device debounce

**Fixed: SOCKS dynamic forwarding failed to start (status bar showed "port forwarding failed: invalid args 'cfg' for command 'pf_start': duplicate field `socks`")** — In v5.0.8 a `dynamic` alias was added to the backend's `socks` field for compatibility with the renderer's legacy field, but serde rejects deserialization as a duplicate field when the standard name and the alias appear **at the same time**; and since v5.0.8 the renderer's new-forwarding config carries both `dynamic` and `socks`, so enabling SOCKS dynamic forwarding and clicking "Start" always failed, and one-click reuse of saved forwarding rules carrying both fields failed the same way. The backend now uses custom deserialization: if either field is true it is dynamic forwarding, fully compatible with all three shapes (`dynamic`+`socks` together, only `dynamic`, only `socks`; zero migration for existing saved rules). Local forwarding is unaffected. Unit tests cover the four field combinations

**Added: Toolbar/quick-command row collapse toggle** — A thin toggle bar has been added below the quick-command row; one click collapses the function row (SFTP/quick commands/port forwarding/split panes/feedback/settings) together with the quick-command row upward and out of sight, letting the terminal area occupy the freed two rows (click again to expand and restore). The arrow is always visible, highlights on hover, and flips with state; the state persists in localStorage and survives restarts. After toggling, the terminal panes automatically re-fit and reflow; it is independent of and stackable with the sidebar collapse toggle, maximizing the terminal area

**Changed: Unified sidebar collapse toggle styling** — The sidebar resize bar width changed from 10px to 6px, the divider line was removed, and the arrow styling was unified with the horizontal resize bar (semi-transparent at rest, highlighted on hover)

**Fixed: After "Finish update" in the online updater, the replacement never ran and the shortcut was refreshed to point at a nonexistent new file ("Windows cannot find \")** — Root causes compounded across three failures in the 5.0.9→5.0.10 upgrade: ① renaming the old exe to .bak was attempted only once before falling back to deferred replacement, and the failure reason never entered the log; ② deferred replacement was an inline one-liner cmd/ping pipeline with no step-by-step logging, popped a GUI error box when the `start` path misbehaved, and had no fallback placement action on failure, making diagnosis impossible; ③ the v5.0.9 shortcut refresh ran **before** the replacement, so after a failed replacement the shortcut pointed to a new-version file that never appeared. Fixed now: .bak rename retries 6×400ms and records the OS error code; deferred replacement is rewritten as a standalone PowerShell script (-File avoids quoting/escaping; waits for the old process to exit ≤30s → renames the backup → places the payload → launches detached → refreshes the shortcut, logging every step to update.log and never popping a GUI box); shortcut refresh now runs **only after the new file is confirmed in place** (on both the in-place and deferred paths)

**Note: this release fixes the "updater executor" itself; users of 5.0.9 and earlier upgrading to 5.0.11 are still upgraded by the old updater (whose deferred-replacement branch keeps the old behavior). If the replacement did not take effect, download 5.0.11 directly from the website and overwrite (config/sessions carry over seamlessly). Updates after 5.0.11 will use the new flow throughout**

**Added: One-click sidebar collapse/expand (click the boundary bar to hide the left sidebar)** — A thin toggle bar has been added at the left edge where the session list meets the terminal area; one click smoothly collapses the left sidebar out of sight and the terminal area fills the freed window space (click again to expand and restore). Collapse/expand animates over 0.18s and the arrow flips with state; the state persists in localStorage and survives restarts. After the sidebar collapses, the terminal panes automatically re-fit and reflow their line counts, and split-pane layouts likewise fill the window

**Added: Quick Launch shortcut generation (requirement change F-R9-01)** — In addition to the existing desktop shortcut, a "Quick Launch" shortcut is now written into the taskbar pinned area (`%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Internet Explorer\Quick Launch\User Pinned\TaskBar\EasySSH.lnk`) and pinned to the taskbar; the pinned-area directory is created automatically as a fallback if missing

**Changed: Desktop/Quick Launch shortcuts are now generated manually on click** — The desktop shortcut that was implicitly generated during upgrade is no longer the only entry point; both shortcut types are now generated by manual clicks under "Settings → Shortcuts" (the backend executes and reports success/failure, same-name .lnk files are overwritten, and repeated clicks are safe)

**Improved: The online update completion flow refreshes both shortcut types automatically** — After the update replaces in a new-version exe, the desktop + Quick Launch shortcuts are refreshed together to point at the new file (run detached so it never blocks the update; failures are silent and do not affect the main update flow)

**Fixed: SOCKS dynamic forwarding broken (browser proxy on 127.0.0.1:<port> had no internet)** — A frontend/backend field-name mismatch in port-forwarding config: the renderer sent `dynamic` while the backend PfConfig only recognized `socks`; after serde silently dropped the unknown field, SOCKS dynamic forwarding was started as an ordinary local forward (empty target host, port 0), so the client's SOCKS5 handshake was immediately dropped with no response. The backend's `socks` field now carries a `dynamic` alias (existing saved forwarding rules in saved sessions and the one-click apply path are fixed in the same change, zero migration), and the renderer additionally sends the standard `socks` field; local forwarding is unaffected. This was introduced by the v5 port-forwarding rewrite (v4 did not have it)

**Fixed: Session-list toolbar buttons overflowed the sidebar** — Adding a 4th "External" button to the tool row exceeded the 230px sidebar width; the layout is now 2×2 wrapping (new group/export/import/external)

**Fixed: Online update "finish update failed: replacement blocked by system/security software"** — A freshly downloaded update package is often briefly locked and scanned by security software (360 etc.); the original replacement flow attempted rename on the new file only once and errored/rolled back on failure. Now hardened: rename retries (6×400ms) → copy fallback (still works when the source is read-only locked) → on persistent failure, automatic rollback to the old version and a deferred-replacement script (waits 10 seconds for scanning to finish before taking over), with the whole process logged (REPLACE_RETRY/REPLACE_DEFERRED); no more false-positive interruptions

**Fixed: Update banner not shown when a new version is found (status bar hinted but no banner/update button)** — A generic `.hidden { display:none !important }` rule introduced by the v5(beta) M3 refactor overrode the banner's inline `display:flex`, and the banner element carried `class="hidden"`; the update flow only changed inline styles and never removed the class, so the banner (and its "download & verify / finish update" buttons) was permanently invisible. Banner show/hide is now unified through show/hide helpers (removing/restoring the .hidden class), covering all paths: auto-detection replay/manual check/download progress/position-anomaly warning/rollback notice/later

**Fixed: After selecting a connection record and clicking "New connection → Cancel", the form kept the filled values** — The cancel button previously only cleared error messages; now a unified resetConnectForm clears host/port/username/password/private key path/passphrase, resets auth method to "password", unlinks the session association (pendingSess) and key-generation area, and returns to a blank initial new-connection state (the "＋ New connection" entry goes through the same reset)

**Added: One-click import of external sessions (Xshell / PuTTY / Termius / OpenSSH config)** — The session list gains an "External" import entry: Xshell automatically reads local Session Manager .xsh files (compatible with multiple NetSarang version directories); PuTTY automatically reads registry sessions (SSH only, read via reg query in a hidden window, no new dependencies); Termius imports its exported JSON (credentials resolved to usernames by id); OpenSSH config imports config files (wildcard Host blocks are skipped automatically). Imports share the same deduplication (host+port+username) and sanitization rules (no passwords) as existing JSON import, and are sorted into source-specific groups automatically

**Added: Custom 1+2 split-pane layout (one large left pane, two small right panes)** — The split-pane menu gains "1+2 layout": the left pane spans two full rows while the right side holds two stacked panes; all three dividers are draggable to adjust ratios (double-click to reset), ratios persist with the layout, and the Ctrl+Shift+D layout cycling includes it

**Requirement-pool closure confirmed** — SFTP large-file resumable transfer (v5 M2 journal checkpoints + journal across restarts + write-protection guard) and auto-reconnect (exponential backoff 2/4/8 seconds, up to 3 attempts, no auto-reconnect on deliberate close) were already implemented in earlier releases; the corresponding feedback items are closed after this round's review. The security-software false-positive item is deferred (a code-signing certificate is needed for a root fix; existing appeal materials / user allowlist guides already provide mitigation)

**Fixed: Session import still failed (only showing "import failed")** — v5.0.6 only fixed the type error of passing a path array, without checking the return structure: the file read returned a raw string while the import logic expected `{ok,data}`, so `!res.ok` was always true and it always said "import failed". The bridge layer now parses the JSON and returns it per contract (with BOM handling and readable error reasons), and the import logic also stays compatible with the legacy string return — double insurance

**Fixed: Update banner not shown when a new version is found** — The `updateLast` bridge returned an internal variable that was never assigned (always null), so on startup replay the already-shown banner was hidden again; it now calls the backend `update_last` to read the real detection result (the status bar and settings page worked all along; only the banner was affected)

**Fixed: Session import erroring with "invalid args `path` for command `read_text_file`"** — After the "Import" dialog switched to multi-select it returned an array of paths, while the file-read command requires a single string, making easyssh-sessions.json exported from v4 unimportable. It now reads the selected (first) file and import works again; import still deduplicates by host+port+username and strips password fields automatically

**Fixed: Blank terminal / dead keyboard after connecting** — The form-connect path never registered the first pane (pane.id/disconnected state missing), so the server banner and prompt didn't render, the status bar wrongly reported disconnected, and keyboard input was swallowed. **Fixed: Hardened the fallback for update-completion timing** — The script waiting for the old process to exit was changed to a **bounded loop (up to ~30 seconds) + taskkill force-termination of the old process on timeout**, completely eliminating the hang where "the old process never exited so the new version never launched and the find window stayed open"; the EBUSY fallback path gained the same force-kill guarantee

**Fixed: Visible ping/tasklist/find console windows popping up during update** — A conflict in cmd creation flags (combining DETACHED_PROCESS with CREATE_NO_WINDOW made subcommands allocate their own visible consoles); now only CREATE_NO_WINDOW is used, so the entire update runs without black windows

**Fixed: After online update, the new filename carried a spurious `-update` suffix** — The update payload filename was EasySSH-<version>-update.exe and version extraction didn't strip the -update suffix, so after updating the new file was wrongly named like EasySSH-4.3.8-update-portable.exe; the suffix is now stripped correctly and the new file is named EasySSH-<version>-portable.exe

**Improved: Real-time download progress percentage for the online update** — The banner's "Downloading encrypted package…" now directly shows the download progress percentage (streaming download, reporting every 256KB/1% increment; previously there was no progress display at all during download)

**Fixed: Online update "download & verify" falsely completed instantly** — The reset event fired at download start mistakenly used the `downloaded` type (empty payload), which the renderer misread as "download complete" and the banner jumped ahead to the "finish update" stage; the real download hadn't finished, so clicking "finish update" reported "new version not yet downloaded". **Fixed: Clicking "finish update" mid-download now gives a clear notice** (download still in progress…) instead of an error

**Fixed: SFTP right-click "Properties" did nothing** — The bridge layer failed to expose the sftp_metadata interface so the call failed silently; it is now exposed with disconnect self-healing; properties open normally for a single selected file/directory
**Fixed: File context menu wrongly showed "Calculate size (directory)"** — That menu item now only appears for directories

**Optimized: SFTP multi-select interaction** — Clicking a row or its checkbox toggles selection (add/remove) directly, so consecutive multi-selection works without holding Ctrl; Shift range selection is preserved

**Added: SFTP properties viewer** — Right-click "Properties" shows a file/directory's name, type, size, modified time, and full path

**Added: Directory size calculation** — Right-click a directory and "Calculate size" recursively tallies its disk usage (depth capped at 40 levels / 200k entries to prevent runaway; unreadable subdirectories are skipped from the count), with results written back into the list for direct viewing; the Properties dialog also offers a "Calculate directory size" button

**Added: SFTP multi-select** — The file list supports selecting multiple files and directories via checkboxes / Ctrl-click / Shift range selection; the multi-select context menu only shows batchable actions (download / delete / properties / refresh), and selection clears automatically on refresh; batch downloads all land in "the chosen directory" (directories recursively, files directly), and batch delete removes items recursively and summarizes the results

**Security hardening: config.key now stored on disk with DPAPI bound to the current user** — The key file changed from 32B of raw unencrypted data to CryptProtectData ciphertext (ESSHDPAPI1 format), so copying config.json+config.key to another user/machine can no longer decrypt saved passwords; legacy unencrypted keys are transparently upgraded on first read; when decryption fails on a new machine it errors clearly with handling guidance and never silently resets

**Security hardening: master password derivation upgraded again to Argon2id (wrap:v3)** — On top of v4.3.0's PBKDF2-600k (wrap:v2), Argon2id (m=64MiB, t=3, p=1) is added as the new write format; all of v1/v2/v3 remain fully compatible and readable
**Security hardening: CSP tightened** — `script-src 'self'` with inline scripts externalized (boot-splash.js / win-controls.js), closing the script-injection surface

**Robustness: Fixed cross-session isolation of SFTP channels (correctness)** — The old implementation's open() reused any channel, so concurrent SFTP across multiple tabs could leak into another session's server; now isolated per session and released on disconnect
**Robustness: SFTP channel self-healing** — After auto-reconnect, dead channels are automatically reopened and retried (covering listing/transfer/delete/rename/mkdir)
**Robustness: Single-instance enforcement** — A second launch just summons the existing window, eliminating corrupted config.json from double-running
**Robustness: Auto-reconnect** — Unexpected disconnects retry automatically with exponential backoff at 2/4/8 seconds, up to 3 attempts; press Enter to take over; deliberate close never triggers it
**Robustness: Automatic fallback to bak.1~bak.5 when config.json fails to read**
**Efficiency: SFTP transfer concurrency gate** — Queued at 4 concurrent by default, so bulk directory transfers no longer hog bandwidth with unbounded concurrency
**Efficiency: Enhanced batched merging of terminal output** — Pushing early at a 32KB threshold + UTF-8 multi-byte cross-chunk truncation protection (on top of the 16ms frame batching)

**Security hardening: Master password derivation strengthened (wrap:v2)** — PBKDF2-SHA256 iterations raised from 100,000 to **600,000** (OWASP 2023 recommendation), greatly increasing the cost of offline password guessing; fully backward-compatible with wrap:v1, **transparently migrated automatically on first unlock**, no action needed

**Robustness: Atomic writes + rolling backups for config.json** — Saving is now atomic via tmp→fsync→rename, eliminating half-written corruption from power loss/crash; the last 5 `config.json.bak.1~5` are kept automatically for rollback; `config.key(.enc)` key-file writes are likewise atomic
**Robustness: panic policy abort→unwind** — Any internal Rust panic no longer hard-crashes outright (losing all sessions/transfers); upper layers can now catch it

**Efficiency: 16ms frame-batched bulk pushing of terminal output** — High-frequency output (cat of large files/top) switched from per-packet IPC to aggregated pushes, sharply cutting IPC count and CPU usage; buffers are flushed before disconnect so trailing output is never lost
**Efficiency: Throttled SFTP transfer progress events** — Changed from every 256KB to 100ms or ≥1% increments, so large-file transfers no longer cause an event storm

**WebView2 cache cleanup pushed down into the Rust startup layer** (a third layer of defense, curing "fixes never take effect"): before window creation, Rust compares the `.ui-cache-ver` marker (version|build timestamp) and deletes the WebView2 data directory directly on mismatch — no longer relying on frontend JS to trigger it (with a buggy old JS the cleanup never happens, and fixes like the SFTP context menu stay stuck behind stale cache); it also takes ownership of the `WebView2Data` user-data directory with a fixed path that is safe to delete

**Automatic cleanup of stale WebView2 cache after updates** (the second layer of defense beyond no-store): on first launch after a version change, it automatically backs up self-created groups/download directory → clears the WebView2 cache and old JS → auto-reloads to recover — guaranteeing that after an update what runs is always the brand-new UI, so fixes like the SFTP dialog/progress overlay always take effect

**Root cause of "some fixes don't take effect on some users' machines" cured**: the Tauri resource protocol responses carried no Cache-Control header, so WebView2 cached index.html/JS/CSS indefinitely by heuristics — multiple versions updating in place shared the same WebView2 user directory, so the app kept loading old cached JS/CSS (new code like the SFTP dialog and progress overlay never actually loaded). A custom resource-protocol handler is now in place and every resource response carries **Cache-Control: no-store**, so fixes take effect immediately after updating
From this release on, all UI fixes land immediately, no longer affected by the WebView2 cache

Fixed the **online update retry loop that kept popping "cannot overwrite install"**: the update payload was previously an install bootstrapper, which rewrote the same-named EasySSH.exe while it was itself running; when locked by the process or security software it looped forever — the payload is now the **MSVC standalone exe** directly (zero extraction; the updater first renames the old exe to free the slot, then writes the new version in place and launches it; no bootstrapper step, no more overwrite conflict)
Fixed the installer bootstrapper notice displaying a literal "\n"

**All builds switched to the official MSVC toolchain**: the unsigned mingw-built exe was falsely flagged by some security software (Trojan.Win64.SilverFox); MSVC builds are the standard Windows toolchain output with a significantly lower false-positive rate; portable standalone exe / installer / portable package all now use MSVC builds
Portable standalone exe is 14.8MB; installer bootstrapper is 6.5MB; the portable package contains only the single-file EasySSH.exe (WebView2Loader.dll no longer needed)
A false-positive appeal with concrete hashes has been submitted to the security vendors

**Dual-display insurance for SFTP upload progress**: on top of the overlay (progress bar), the SFTP panel's message line also shows text progress "⬆ Uploading xx% (transferred/total) filename" (visible at any display layer), with "✅ Upload complete" on finish
**Delete confirmation now uses the native system dialog** (Tauri dialog plugin, no longer relying on any self-drawn styling); the new-directory input keeps the self-drawn dialog

Fixed **SFTP upload progress overlay not showing** (root cause): the overlay's inline z-index:60 was below the modal backdrop's z-index:100, so it was covered by the backdrop — changed to 150 and verified through the real rendering pipeline (display/z-index/bar/percentage all correct)
Fixed **transfer queue count always 0**: the progress event's taskId field did not match the renderer's, now aligned

Fixed **network adapters (LAN IP) not collected**: GetAdaptersAddresses had a bound parameter type error (Family mistakenly declared as u16); rewritten with the standard structure — adapters (name/MAC/LAN IPv4) now report correctly
Fixed **public IP shown as raw JSON** (e.g. {"ip":"1.2.3.4"}): all endpoint responses are now uniformly parsed and validated (supports JSON-wrapped or plain-text, with IPv4-segment/IPv6 validation)
Deduplicated GPU enumeration (duplicate same-name virtual GPUs under RDP sessions are no longer listed repeatedly)
Added a race-condition fallback to the SFTP transfer progress overlay (progress bar shows correctly even when a small file finishes instantly)

Fixed **repeated "Error opening file for writing" when the installer version overwrites an existing install**: when the target EasySSH.exe is in use (app running or temporarily locked by security software), the default NSIS error dialog only retries mechanically. Now: if the file is in use, the old file is automatically renamed first to free the slot (if still locked, a dialog prompts "Please exit EasySSH first" and retry); when writing is blocked by security software, clear guidance is shown (wait for the scan to finish and retry / temporarily disable the security software), with retries available throughout until success

Fixed **security software blocking PowerShell when submitting feedback**: the PowerShell subprocess collection was removed entirely and replaced with **pure native WinAPI collection** (direct registry reads + system calls, no subprocesses, no script execution — zero interception by security software) — all collected fields fully preserved (OS/CPU/memory/motherboard/GPU/disk/network adapter MAC+IP/public IP with multi-endpoint redundancy/uptime/system language)

**Public egress IP collection now uses multi-endpoint redundancy**: primary endpoint ip.263.tw/ip, fallbacks in order ipify / ifconfig.me / icanhazip / ipecho (each with a 5-second timeout + IP shape validation, skipped only if all fail), greatly improving collection success on weak networks
Release process: the dist/release directory automatically keeps only the latest 3 versions (cleanup built into the build script)

Fixed **manually running the single-file launcher did not overwrite the old version**: when a complete program already existed in the directory, the launcher skipped extraction and started the old version — it now **always overwrites on extraction** (the old EasySSH.exe is renamed to .old before writing the new version, then the new version starts; the app cleans up .old on next launch)

Fixed **nothing visible during startup** (blank window during ~2-3 seconds of WebView2 initialization): the window now shows immediately at startup with a dark background color (Tauri backgroundColor), paired with a splash animation — visual feedback from double-click to main UI, no blank screen
Added a 15-second fallback to hide the splash (no longer stuck on the splash if front-end initialization fails)

Extended **computer/network info collection in feedback** (matching and exceeding the 3.x scope): OS version (build), CPU model/cores/threads, memory size, motherboard, GPU, local disks (size/free), **network adapter (MAC/LAN IPv4)**, **public egress IP**, system uptime, system language, hostname — collection runs in a single PowerShell pass (windowless in background, per-item fault tolerance, finishes within seconds), public IP via ipify (5-second timeout, skipped automatically on failure); the website feedback console and patrol emails display all fields

Fixed **the single-file launcher extracting into an EasySSH\\ subdirectory**: it now deploys flat — the program is extracted directly into the launcher's own directory (current directory), so EasySSH.exe and WebView2Loader.dll land in place and existing config.json/config.key/keys/connection records are reused as-is; when a complete program already exists, double-clicking again skips extraction and launches instantly

Fixed **SFTP "New directory" and "Delete" not working**: they used window.prompt / window.confirm, unsupported by WebView2 (silently returning empty so the operation was skipped) — replaced with custom-drawn input/confirm dialogs (Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel); the master password reset confirmation was fixed the same way

Fixed **SFTP transfer progress overlay not showing**: the overlay's z-index was below the modal backdrop and was covered; raised above the modal — upload/download progress bar and percentage now display normally

Fixed **no response when clicking upload file**: the upload task mistakenly queried remote metadata (a new file does not exist yet and always errors); uploads now take the local file size and downloads the remote size

Added **SFTP transfer progress overlay**: after choosing a file to upload or double-clicking to download, a semi-transparent progress layer appears, showing per-file progress bars and percentages (with transferred/total size); ✅ is shown on completion and the layer auto-dismisses, failures/cancellations show the reason — the overlay stays visible for the duration of the transfer

Fixed **no silent new-version check at startup and no automatic periodic check** (the upgrade banner only appeared via manual "Check for updates" on the settings page): the automatic check rules from 3.x were omitted in the v4 Rust rewrite and are now restored — a silent check 3 seconds after startup, then automatically every 1 hour while running; when a new version is found, a top upgrade banner appears (same behavior as 3.x)
Fixed **custom title-bar window control symbols (─ □ ✕) not centered** (default button padding and text baseline offset pushed the symbols right): switched to flex centering and removed padding

Fixed **online update extracting into the wrong EasySSH\EasySSH subdirectory** (the v4.0.6 update payload was a single-file launcher; after in-place updates 4.0.x users were led into a subdirectory layout, making connection records/configuration appear "lost"): the updater now launches the launcher with the --upgraded argument; the launcher recognizes upgrade mode and performs an **overwrite install in the original directory** — the running old exe is renamed to .old, the new EasySSH.exe and WebView2Loader.dll are extracted over it, and the app starts in place; config.json/config.key/keys are all preserved, so connection records are no longer lost; in-place upgrades for 3.x (Electron) users are also handled (overwriting EasySSH.exe inside the Electron directory and adding WebView2Loader.dll)
Leftover update backups (EasySSH.exe.old / .bak) are cleaned up automatically at app startup

Optimized **the layout of the "Check for updates" message in Settings**: the status line now keeps only a brief result (e.g. "New version v4.0.7 found (current 4.0.6)"), and the long update details moved to a dedicated full-width area below (above the "Check automatically at startup…" description line) instead of being squeezed into the narrow strip beside the button

Fixed **SFTP directories could not be entered by double-click / files could not be downloaded by double-click**: remote entries lacked a type field (the renderer distinguishes behavior by type==='dir'/'file'); sftp_list now returns type; SFTP rename/delete/new-directory results return a structured ok (previously null was misreported as failure by the renderer)
Fixed **port forwarding record names showing undefined**: pf_start configuration now includes a name field, returned in the running-list snapshot

Fixed **SFTP failing to open with missing sftpId / uploads not responding**: the SFTP channel is now lazily opened per session and cached (previously the session id was passed as the SFTP channel id to file-operation commands); the upload file dialog's multi-select behavior was restored
Fixed **pressing F5 / Ctrl+R refreshing the whole page and disconnecting sessions** (WebView2 browser accelerator keys, now intercepted)

Fixed **some UI receiving the encrypted password after enabling the master password**: config reading now uses the in-process unwrapped DEK (config.key can still be decrypted normally after being renamed to .bak, matching 3.x getDek behavior)

Fixed **port forwarding "unknown error" and SFTP "missing sftpId"**: corrected bridge-layer return-value semantics (success/failure wrapped in the ok/message structure the renderer expects) and lazy per-session SFTP channel opening
Master password "enable/change/disable" no longer misreport "operation failed" on success (command return values aligned with the renderer's checks)

Fixed **"upgrade response validation failed" when checking for updates**: envelope MAC verification incorrectly compared hex against base64 strings (the protocol's mac field is base64); now decoded and compared in constant time

Fixed **master password "enable/change/disable" not responding**: the masterpw_* command family was not registered to IPC; the master password dialog's layer was also raised above the settings dialog (it was previously hidden behind it)

Fixed **unable to read private keys**: an empty passphrase was passed to the decryptor for keys without one (russh reported "private key is already decrypted"); passphrase-less keys are now handled as unencrypted

Fixed **"upgrade key not configured" when checking updates or submitting feedback**: the v4 installer did not carry update-keys.json; official builds now embed the upgrade master key at build time (placing an update-keys.json next to the exe still overrides), restoring the update and feedback channels
Fixed **startup status bar showing version "v—"**: the version number is now prefetched asynchronously and backfilled

Fixed **key authentication taking the wrong branch**: renderer connection parameters lacked the authtype field (in 3.x semantics, providing privateKey meant key mode); v4.0.0 misjudged it as password mode and authenticated with an empty password, so key logins reported "server rejected username/password". The auth branch is now decided by "whether privateKey is provided" (if provided, key auth plus a keyboard-interactive fallback only, never falling back to an empty password); the reconnect path behaves the same

**All-new v4.0.0 kernel officially released (Tauri 2 rewrite)**: Rust + system WebView2 replace Electron — the portable zip dropped from 98.4MB to **9.4MB (-90%)**, the exe from 181MB to 32MB, instant startup, halved memory usage, and a greatly reduced false-positive surface for security software (no DLLs written to disk, no scripts)

**Seamless config migration**: config.json / config.key / config.key.enc / master password protocol are fully compatible with 3.x — copy config.json and config.key (or config.key.enc) from your 3.x program directory into the v4 directory to keep all sessions and stored passwords
**UI**: identical to 3.x (custom title bar + window control buttons, same colors); feedback submissions automatically carry the software version number
