Implemented as a lightweight i18n layer (a dictionary keyed by Simplified Chinese strings + text-node traversal + dynamic message listeners for auto-translation), covering all settings, connection, SFTP, port forwarding, quick command, feedback, master password, and online update UI text (~210 strings × 4 languages); user data such as session names/notes/quick commands is never translated; technical diagnostics output inside the terminal remains Chinese for now and will be completed in a later version

Changed **zip portable package slimming (111.7MB → 98.4MB)**: language packs keep only the 4 UI-supported ones (en-US / zh-CN / zh-TW / ko, previously 100+ languages taking 41MB); removed the full Chromium third-party licenses HTML (MIT LICENSE kept; license details on the website's license.html); removed the software Vulkan fallback components (vk_swiftshader / vulkan-1.dll, only a WebGL fallback for extreme no-GPU environments, imperceptible for a terminal app). The trimmed zip is now under 100MB and can be uploaded directly to Gitee

Changed **discontinued the single-file exe distribution; only the zip portable package remains**: the single-file launcher (first-run self-extraction + NSIS launcher) repeatedly triggered security software false positives for "modifying critical program DLL files" (the signature of an unsigned NSIS launcher extracting runtime files such as d3dcompiler_47.dll plus the app loading that DLL could not be fully mitigated even with installer UI and version resources; a real fix requires a code-signing certificate). The website and GitHub/Gitee downloads now offer only the zip portable package — extract and run; **the online update channel is unaffected** (the encrypted payload is now the app's own EasySSH.exe, replacing `EasySSH\EasySSH.exe` in place, with icon and version consistent with the exe after update); existing users of the single-file launcher: keep it only as a launch entry (double-clicking it starts the latest version in the adjacent EasySSH\ folder), or delete the launcher exe and use a desktop shortcut instead; the website download page copy and SHA256 verification example were updated to zip accordingly

Fixed **the launcher-deployed `EasySSH\EasySSH.exe` still showing the Electron atom icon**: with `signAndEditExecutable:false`, electron-builder does not rewrite exe resources, so the exe in win-unpacked kept the original Electron icon and the launcher deployed it as-is to user machines (the folder zip build used electron-packager and had a correct icon, which is why this went unnoticed). The build process now uses pure-JS resedit/pe-library (no wine required) to write the blue lightning icon + version resources (product name/company/version) into the win-unpacked exe; icons are now consistent across the single-file build, folder build, taskbar, and desktop shortcuts

Mitigated **security software false positives** (security software reporting "a program is trying to modify critical program DLL files", blocking the launcher from extracting d3dcompiler_47.dll and other Electron runtime files): the single-file launcher abandoned `SilentInstall` silent mode (silent DLL drops are a high-risk heuristic signature) in favor of a **standard installer look with a progress UI** (window title "EasySSH 安装程序", detailed installation steps); the exe now includes full VS_VERSIONINFO version resources (product name/company/version/website) so security software and system properties can identify its official identity; directories already deployed still launch instantly on double-click (the window auto-hides without bothering you). User-side whitelist guidance is also provided (see the website FAQ / README)

Refactored **the single-file exe into a "first-run self-extracting installer"** (replacing the old portable mode that extracted to %TEMP% on every start, fixing slow startup and special-cased updates):

First double-click of `EasySSH-<version>.exe`: extracts the full application into an **`EasySSH\` folder next to the exe**, automatically creates a desktop shortcut (pointing to `EasySSH\EasySSH.exe`), and starts the app;

Afterwards, double-clicking the single-file exe or the desktop shortcut: **launches the folder version directly, instant start** — no more extracting ~200MB to %TEMP% each time, and no more repeated security-software scans of temp extractions;

**Online update is now fully unified with the zip folder version**: process and files share one directory; downloads are saved to `EasySSH\updates\` and after exit the `EasySSH.exe` that the desktop shortcut points to is replaced in place — no more temp downloads, anchor resolution, or EBUSY special cases (the v3.0.1–3.0.3 protection logic remains as a compatibility path for users of the old single-file version);
Still fully portable: no registry writes, no admin rights required, and the whole `EasySSH\` folder can be copied to any computer;
The folder zip version now recreates a missing desktop shortcut at runtime (main.js `ensureDesktopShortcut()`).

Fixed **Windows taskbar icon differing from the desktop icon**: the main process did not set an icon when creating the BrowserWindow, so taskbar/window icons showed the default Electron atom instead of the blue lightning desktop icon; the window icon now explicitly points to `icon.ico`, making the taskbar, Alt+Tab, and window title bar consistent with the desktop icon

Fixed **single-file version's online update "Finish update" failing to replace with EBUSY**: the single-file exe (NSIS launcher) stays alive while running and locks its own file, so renaming the old exe to .bak always failed with EBUSY. The update module now first detects the run mode (single-file portable / folder zip version): downloads always go to the real installation directory (for the single-file version, the directory containing PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_FILE, with the installation directory anchor also recorded in userData — never into temp; if even the anchor cannot be resolved, the download is explicitly refused); replacement first renames in place with retries, and if the file is still locked, falls back automatically to "delayed replace after exit" (built-in cmd commands only, no bat files written to disk, avoiding security-software false positives): after this process and the launcher exit and release the lock, cmd performs old version backup to .bak → new version takes the original name → new version auto-starts, with the desktop shortcut carried over seamlessly

Fixed **upgrading from a temp-directory copy still "replaced in place" the temp copy**: during the v3.0.0→v3.0.1 online update, "Finish update" replaced and started the extracted copy in %TEMP% (e.g. C:\Users\…\AppData\Local\Temp) while the old version in the actual installation directory (e.g. P:\Program Files (x86)\EasySSH) was untouched; afterwards, upgrades initiated from the temp copy still downloaded the package into the temp directory. The update module now checks at startup whether the current exe resides in the system temp directory (`isTempResident()`): if it does, the upgrade banner clearly warns "this update cannot replace the real installation directory", **in-place replacement is refused**, and manual fix guidance is given (close the app → move the new exe back into the installation directory over the old one, or re-download from easyssh.cn) — no more creating the illusion of a "successful upgrade"

Fixed **online update downloading and replacing in entirely wrong locations in the portable version**: previously the download directory came from `app.getPath('exe')`, but in the portable version the process runs from a %TEMP% extraction directory, so the package landed in `Temp\...\updates`; the replacement step mistakenly used the `PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_PATH` environment variable, which does not exist (the actual injected variable is `PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_FILE`), so "Finish update" renamed, replaced, and relaunched the temp copy while the old version double-clicked on the desktop was untouched. Now `realExePath()` (PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_FILE → fallback) locates the real exe consistently: the package is downloaded into an **updates\\ subdirectory of the directory containing the running software**, and "Finish update" completes the replacement in the original directory — old version renamed to .bak → new version takes the original name → new version started detached — with the desktop shortcut carried over seamlessly and the .bak backup available for rollback

Added **master password protection**: optional to enable; when enabled, config.key is wrapped with a passphrase-derived key (PBKDF2 100,000 iterations + AES-256-GCM) into config.key.enc, and the unencrypted key is never written to disk — even if config.json and config.key are both copied away, session passwords cannot be recovered without the master password. A full-screen unlock prompt appears at startup with at most 5 wrong attempts; saving sessions is refused while locked, preventing blank-password overwrites; changing/disabling the master password is supported

Added **forgot-password escape path**: after 5 failed attempts you can reset — clearing the master password and all stored passwords (session list/groups/notes/fingerprints all preserved, passwords re-entered), with a clear notice that this is irreversible; this is itself a security feature, not a flaw

Added **host fingerprint verification (anti-MITM)**: the first connection shows a SHA256 fingerprint (OpenSSH style) to confirm and save; subsequent connections compare automatically, and on mismatch the SSH handshake is rejected outright with a dialog showing "stored vs actual" and a MITM warning, with options to update the fingerprint and reconnect or cancel; fingerprints are stored in config.json and contain no sensitive information — you get stopped before connecting to a spoofed server
**Zero migration for existing users**: without the master password enabled, behavior is identical to the old version

Added **session logging**: a settings toggle + directory (empty = logs/ in the program directory), recording remote output (not keyboard input) to a host-date.log file per connection, with a separator written and the file closed automatically on disconnect — troubleshooting server issues and reviewing command results no longer requires scrolling back by eye

Added **terminal find**: Ctrl+F or the toolbar 🔍 opens a find bar; Enter/Shift+Enter jump up/down, an n/n counter is shown, and Esc clears highlights (based on @xterm/addon-search 0.14.0) — no more paging through tens of thousands of lines to find one error
Added **configurable scrollback**: three settings tiers of 5000/10000/50000, applied instantly to open terminals — big tasks that need more history are no longer truncated at the 5000-line cap

Added **copy/paste enhancements**: copy on selection (optional toggle), right-click paste, Ctrl+Shift+C/V shortcuts; the Ctrl+C interrupt signal is unaffected — users used to local terminal habits no longer need the repeated "select → right-click copy → right-click paste" cycle
**Backward compatibility with old config.json**: missing new settings fields get default values automatically, so no manual config changes are needed after upgrading

Added **SFTP transfer queue**: uploads/downloads now go through a background queue with multiple files running in parallel; the dialog shows a live progress bar, speed, current file, and multi-file count per task; queued tasks can be **cancelled mid-transfer** along with "clear completed"; the SFTP panel gains a live "⇅ Queue N" badge and the header gains a transfer queue entry — bulk transfers no longer freeze the dialog, and you no longer wait file by file

Added **recursive directory transfer**: upload/download an entire folder (including subdirectories) in one click, with remote directories created level by level automatically — transferring a project directory no longer requires manually mkdir-ing on the server first and uploading layer by layer

Added **resume** (single-file downloads, binary mode): after a network interruption, transfer continues from the breakpoint instead of starting over — multi-GB file transfers no longer go to waste on a mid-transfer disconnect
Added **drag-and-drop upload**: drag local files/folders straight into the SFTP panel to enqueue uploads automatically, skipping repeated clicks on "Upload" and file selection

Added **remote file context menu**: supports Download / Rename / New directory / Delete (directory delete includes all contents, with a confirmation prompt) / Refresh — remote file management no longer requires typing commands

Added **session group management**: the left connection list supports creating groups, moving sessions into groups, and collapsing/expanding groups, with the ungrouped "Default" pinned at the top — no more scrolling endlessly through one long list once your servers multiply
Added **session search**: live filtering by host/name/note, so dozens of sessions can be located in one go

Added **notes and tab colors**: sessions can carry notes (small gray text in the list + hover tooltip) and a choice of 6 preset colors (color dot in the list + colored tab title, with open tabs updated live) — tell production from test at a glance and avoid connecting to the wrong server

Added **session import/export**: exported JSON automatically strips passwords and passphrases (including encrypted ciphertext fields); imports are deduplicated by host+port+username with a count of skipped duplicates, and imported sessions without passwords need re-entry — migrating to a new machine or sharing configs with a team no longer means copying entries by hand
Added **session cloning**: one right-click copies a session's configuration with the name suffixed "- copy" — duplicating a similar server only requires changing the IP

Improved the **feedback** feature: submissions are more reliable and official troubleshooting is faster; the website's feedback console was enhanced in parallel (batch deletion, paginated management, a clearer admin interface)

Added **user feedback**: a new "💬 Feedback" button in the app toolbar; feedback content is submitted to the website easyssh.cn as an AES-256-GCM encrypted envelope (same protocol family as the online update, key derived from the update master key, no new key file); includes time-bound signatures (±15 minutes anti-replay), content length validation, and rate limiting (5 per IP per hour, 60-second spacing)

The website gains a **feedback admin console** (feedback-admin.html, admin username/password login): create/delete/edit feedback, official replies, and a toggle for publishing to the front end; the download page adds a "Featured user feedback" section showing the top 10 replied-and-published items

Website **download page**: a popup link "For more historical versions see GitHub or Gitee" was added below the historical versions table; the GitHub / Gitee links in the site-wide footer now open in popups

Website **homepage**: the hero was replaced with a real app screenshot (AVIF 20KB + WebP fallback, 70% smaller than the original 66KB) plus lightweight entrance, hover, sheen-sweep, and cursor-blink animations (respecting prefers-reduced-motion)

Added **edit/delete/one-click reuse for port forwarding records**: previously the port forwarding dialog showed only running forwards, and forwarding configs saved with a session were invisible after reconnecting or when not started, making them unusable. The dialog now also lists "saved but not running" records — ▶ restart in one click, ✎ edit (config back-filled into the form; saving writes back to the session automatically, and running forwards restart with the new config), ✕ delete (removed from the session config for real); running forwards likewise support ✎ edit and ✕ stop

Fixed **clicking "＋ New connection" doing nothing when connections already exist**: the button's click event was never bound, and switching to an existing connection tab hid the new-connection panel, so it could never be opened again. Clicking the button now re-shows the new-connection panel, clears the last error, and focuses the host input, so a second connection can be opened
Widened the port forwarding dialog (420px→720px, height 520px); inputs were widened and adapt to the width, eliminating horizontal scrolling and buttons pushed out of the dialog

Fixed **"Finish update" reporting "target version is not higher than current version, replacement refused (anti-downgrade)", making online updates fail forever**: the update manifest's file entries never carried a `version` field, so after download the version was empty and the anti-downgrade comparison treated the empty string as a lower version and refused to replace. The client now completes the version from the check result, with a fallback parsing it from the file name `EasySSH-<version>.exe`; when the version still cannot be determined, a clear prompt tells you to run the new version manually instead of misreporting "anti-downgrade"
The server-side update manifest now also includes the `version` field in file entries (belt and braces)

Security hardening: **server passwords in config.json are now stored encrypted** (AES-256-GCM). On first run, a random master key file `config.key` (0600 permissions) is generated in the same directory as the exe; the `passphrase` of both password sessions and key sessions is persisted in the format `enc:v1:<iv>:<tag>:<ciphertext>`, unencrypted data only ever exists in memory and is decrypted on read. Non-sensitive fields such as the key session's private key path are unaffected; reading old unencrypted configs still works and they are automatically upgraded to ciphertext on the next save. **Note: `config.key` and `config.json` must be carried/backed up together — copying config.json alone will make the passwords unrecoverable**

Fixed the website's "Feature Overview" page showing a chunk of raw Markdown badge code at the top (README's GitHub release/website/License badge lines were being treated as body text by the sync tool) — the sync tool now automatically skips badge lines

Added **SOCKS 4/5 dynamic forwarding for port forwarding** (same as SecureCRT's "Use SOCKS 4 or 5 dynamic forwarding"): the port forwarding dialog now has a checkbox; when checked, no remote host/port is needed — the local port becomes a dynamically forwarded port through the SSH encrypted tunnel (supports SOCKS5 unauthenticated CONNECT (IPv4/domain/IPv6) and SOCKS4/4a). Point a browser or program (`curl --socks5` etc.) at `127.0.0.1:<port>` to reach any target reachable by the SSH server
SOCKS dynamic forwarding config persists with the session: forwarding stops automatically when the connection drops and is restored automatically on reconnect

Fixed **Settings Center having no download entry after "Check for Updates" finds a new version**: previously only the top banner had "Download & Verify / Finish Upgrade" buttons; the settings dialog now shows the same download/finish-upgrade buttons, kept in real-time sync with the banner (download progress, failure reason, and completion notice are visible on both)

Added **application icon**: a multi-size icon (16/24/32/48/256) designed after the lightning logo in the UI's top-right corner — dark rounded base with a blue-cyan gradient lightning bolt, now embedded in the exe file icon and taskbar

Fixed **"Finish Upgrade" doing nothing when clicked**: ① when running the portable single-file version, the process lives in a %TEMP% extraction directory, and the old logic replaced the temporary copy instead of the real exe the user double-clicked (now uses PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_PATH to locate the real file); ② the failure reason was only written to the settings dialog's notice area while it was closed, giving no visible feedback (the failure reason and manual fix path are now shown directly on the top banner)

Added **quick command editing**: each entry in the "Quick Command Manager" dialog now has a ✎ Edit button; clicking it fills the name/command back into the bottom input fields and turns the "Add" button into "Save"; saving updates the entry in place and refreshes the toolbar quick command bar; deleting the entry being edited or reopening the dialog cancels edit mode; the input fields support Enter to submit

Fixed **existing users not seeing the default quick commands**: the default seeding logic lived in loadConfig's "first-run migration" branch, but existing users already have a config.json and always read it via an early return before that branch, so the seeding code never ran. Seeding has been moved to a spot both read paths pass through (works for existing config files too, still injected only once)

Added **local port forwarding** (modeled on SecureCRT's Session Options → Connection → Port Forwarding): once the SSH session is established, the program opens forwarding on the specified port at local 127.0.0.1, and traffic to that port is relayed through the encrypted tunnel by the SSH server to "target host:target port" (leave the target empty for the SSH server itself, or point it at other machines on the intranet reachable from the server) — typical uses: securely accessing intranet databases, intranet web admin consoles, and other services only reachable via the jump host

Toolbar now has "🔀 Port Forwarding": add/stop forwarding for the current active connection directly, with a live list of "local 127.0.0.1:<local port> → target host:target port"; errors such as a local port already in use or remote refusal are echoed directly to the terminal

Forwarding config persists with the session: remembered when the session is saved, forwarding is automatically restarted on the next connection (including reconnects after a drop); all forwarding stops automatically when the session disconnects

Implementation notes: built on ssh2's forwardOut (forwarded-tcpip channel) with the local socket wired byte-for-byte to the channel; verified end-to-end against a local sshd (full SSH handshake completed through the tunnel)

Fixed **default quick commands not visible after upgrading from older versions**: the old settings file already contained an empty quickCommands array, which overrode the newly added defaults. A "seeded" flag is now introduced — defaults are injected only once for users who never had quick commands and the flag is set, so they don't come back after the user deletes them all
Fixed **wrong version number in the status bar**: the version was a hard-coded constant (stuck at v2.3.5); it now reads the app's real version live from the main process at startup

Added **default common quick commands**: on first use (if quick commands were never customized), 10 ops-common commands are built in — system info/disk usage/memory usage/load/view ports/resource-hungry processes/recent logins/network reachability/restart sshd/clear screen; existing customizations are fully preserved
Website download list **now keeps only the latest 3 versions**: publishing a new version automatically replaces the oldest one (the online upgrade API and update history are unaffected)

**Fix log for the key-login reconnect issue** (cumulative v2.5.1–v2.5.6): ① the upgrade manifest now includes the kind field with backward compatibility for old manifests (fixing "Check for Updates always says up to date"); ② diagnostics fixed two blind spots (false positive public key verification after restart, sshd logs drowned by password entries), plus a server authorized_keys fingerprint comparison and local private key fingerprint display; ③ root-cause fix: connection params didn't save authtype, so pressing Enter to reconnect treated key connections as empty-password connections; authtype is now saved and the main process automatically routes legacy params carrying privateKey through the key branch. All verified end-to-end against a local sshd (generate→install→login chain works)

Fixed **reconnecting by pressing Enter after a key connection drops always failing**: the saved connection params omitted the authtype field, so on reconnect the main process received no auth method and treated the key connection as a password connection (empty password), reporting "All configured authentication methods failed". authtype is now saved in connection params, and the main process automatically routes legacy params without authtype but with privateKey through the key branch (compatible with previously saved sessions)

Added **main-process parameter echo diagnostics**: when a key connection fails, the error now directly shows the authtype/privateKey/password parameters the main process received and which auth branch was actually taken — for locating parameter-loss issues like "the UI selected private-key auth but the main process tried password auth"

Fixed **"Download & Verify" appearing to do nothing when clicked**: download progress/failure info was written to the notice area inside the settings dialog, which is usually closed when the banner button is triggered, so the user saw no change. Download progress, decrypt/verify progress, failure reasons, and the manual download URL are now shown directly on the top update banner

Added **local private key fingerprint display on key-login failure**: the error includes the actual private key path loaded and its SHA256 fingerprint (matching ssh-keygen -lf); comparing it against each server authorized_keys fingerprint immediately shows whether the public/private keys are mismatched (typical case: the installed version and portable version use different keys/ directories, so a different private key was loaded)

Fixed connection failure details being truncated by the UI: the full "local private key loaded" info and ssh2 handshake trace are now shown (previously only the first line appeared and debug info was discarded)
Diagnostic log filtering now excludes Accepted entries, keeping only real rejections/errors

Fixed **"Check for Updates" always reporting up to date**: the client requires manifest entries to carry a `kind:'exe'` field, but the website manifest lacked it, so no installer matched and it was judged "up to date". It now falls back to recognizing files by the `.exe` name (compatible with old and new manifests), and the website sync tool also writes the `kind` field now

Fixed **two blind spots in key-login auto diagnostics**: ① after an app restart, diagnostics no longer carried the UI public-key variable, so `grep -cF ''` falsely reported "public key already written" — it now falls back to reading keys/id_ed25519_easyssh.pub for real verification; ② when grabbing sshd logs, root's password-login entries crowded out key-rejection entries (`Failed publickey`), creating the illusion of "no obvious config problem" — it now filters only rejection/error entries, widens to the last 200 lines, and adds a journalctl source

Added **server authorized_keys fingerprint comparison**: diagnostics now list the SHA256 fingerprints of each public key on the server for comparison against the local public key; a mismatch prompts reinstalling the public key (verified end-to-end against a local sshd: generate/format/signing/login chain all work; rejections were server-side public key mismatch or permission issues)

Added **online upgrade**: "Check for Updates" in the app connects directly to the website's encrypted API `https://easyssh.cn/api/update/check`; when a new version is found it downloads the encrypted installer (dual verification: AES-256-GCM + SHA-256). After download verification passes, clicking "Finish Upgrade" has the old process swap files in place before exiting (old exe renamed to `.bak` → new exe takes over → new version launched detached), script-free throughout with automatic rollback if blocked; leftover `.bak` files and downloads are cleaned up at startup
From this version, upgrades are supported only within this channel's version range (`MIN_UPGRADE_VERSION = 2.5.0`); earlier versions should download and install manually

Fixed: **further hardening of key login still failing after installing the public key in v2.3.4** — public key installation now writes according to the server's actual sshd config: it first reads `AuthorizedKeysFile` from `sshd -T`; if it's a non-default path (e.g. `/etc/ssh/keys/%u`, common on customized systems/all-in-one appliances), the key is written there instead of the default `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` (writing to the wrong place means the public key never takes effect)

Added **automatic diagnosis of key login failures**: when key authentication fails and the server still has a live password connection, the tool automatically collects the real cause on the server — sshd public-key auth switch/AuthorizedKeysFile/PermitRootLogin/multi-step auth config, home directory and key file permissions and ownership, SELinux status, whether the public key was actually written, and rejection entries in sshd logs — and shows item-by-item conclusions directly in the connection panel instead of blindly retrying

The install command is now fault-tolerant per segment: a failure in any segment (e.g. unwritable directory) is caught by read-back verification and the server's error is shown verbatim, eliminating "false success"

Fixed: **"Install to the currently connected server" succeeding but key login still reporting "All configured authentication methods failed"** — the old install command only set ~/.ssh and authorized_keys permissions; when the server's home directory (e.g. /root) is group/world-writable, sshd StrictModes silently refuses to read authorized_keys; SELinux systems (CentOS/RHEL) may also refuse due to wrong context. Installing the public key now automatically runs `chmod g-w,o-w ~` and `restorecon -R ~/.ssh` (when restorecon exists), verifies by read-back that the public key was really written, and detects the server's public-key auth switch via `sshd -T`

If the server's sshd has `PubkeyAuthentication no`, it now clearly prompts after install that public-key auth must be enabled in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and sshd restarted, instead of "install succeeded" yet still unable to log in
The Chinese key-auth failure message was updated in sync, guiding the user to re-run "Install to the currently connected server" to fix permissions

Fixed: **key connections could not be saved as sessions** — "Save Session" only worked for password auth; key-auth connections were lost after restart, and clicking a connection record on the left only restored password mode, requiring the key to be regenerated/refilled. Key connections are now saved too (recording auth method, private key path, passphrase); after restart, clicking a connection record restores "private key file" mode and fills the key path, ready to connect

Fixed: **"One-click local keypair generation" overwrote the existing keypair under keys/ every time**, making the old public key in the server's authorized_keys no longer match the new private key. It now reuses the existing keypair when one is detected instead of regenerating

Fixed: **connection reporting "Cannot parse privateKey: Unsupported key format" after one-click key generation** — ssh2's key parser doesn't support PKCS#8 ("BEGIN PRIVATE KEY") format, but the one-click generated private key was PKCS#8 since v2.3.0, making login with the generated key impossible
Private keys are now generated in standard OpenSSH format ("openssh-key-v1", unencrypted), directly usable by ssh2 (verified via a full SSH handshake signature + ssh-keygen check)

Automatic compatibility with old key files when connecting: PKCS#8 private keys (Ed25519/RSA/EC) generated by older versions are detected and converted to an ssh2-parsable format, so old keys keep working without regeneration

Fixed: the v2.3.0 key info area's stylesheet wasn't bundled (it was mistakenly written to a directory outside the project), squeezing and scrambling the generated results UI — the stylesheet has been put back in place with a width constraint; buttons/info area now fill the panel's full row
Added **key login**:
Selecting "private key file" as the auth method reveals a key tools area; one-click local Ed25519 keypair generation (standard OpenSSH public key format + PKCS#8 private key, directly usable by ssh2)
The private key path auto-fills after generation; the public key content is shown, copyable, and can be manually uploaded to the server's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

"Install to the currently connected server": one click writes the public key to the server via the current password connection (idempotent, with permission setup 700/600); after that you can switch to private key login
Keys are stored under keys/ next to the exe, carried along with the folder

Smarter connection failure messages: auth failure/timeout/connection refused each get tailored troubleshooting advice (auth failure prompts re-entering the password and explains the saved-session password override mechanism)

Fixed: the v2.2.0 custom title bar rework turned the main layout vertical (sidebar jumped to the top) — the sidebar and main area are re-wrapped in a horizontal container, restoring the classic left-right layout
Removed the duplicate EasySSH brand title in the sidebar (the top title bar already covers it)
Themes now apply globally: colors cover the entire app UI (sidebar/toolbar/dialogs/status bar/quick command bar), not just the terminal window

**Title bar follows the theme**: the window now uses a custom-drawn title bar (titleBarOverlay); the top title bar is draggable and window control button colors follow the theme (each of the 5 themes has its own palette)
**Config file consolidation**: sessions.json and settings.json merged into a single **config.json** (cleaner for the portable build); old files migrate automatically, no manual action needed
Added SFTP **encoding-aware transfer**: transfer mode can be "Binary (as-is, recommended)" or "Text conversion"

Text conversion follows the configured encoding: download converts server encoding→UTF-8 (line endings unified to CRLF); upload converts UTF-8→server encoding (line endings unified to LF), with temporary files cleaned up automatically
Added SFTP file transfer panel: browse remote directories, upload files (multi-select), double-click to download, parent directory/path navigation
Added quick command bar: custom command buttons that send to the current terminal on click, with add/remove management
Added Settings Center: fonts (5), font size, encoding (UTF-8/GBK/GB18030/Big5; GBK-family fixes garbled text on Chinese servers), themes (Dracula/Pure Black/Solarized/Light/Matrix)
Added the iconv-lite dependency; settings persist to settings.json
Build artifacts now include the version number in their filenames; README establishes a version history system
Added: the tab is kept after the SSH session exits/drops, **pressing Enter in the terminal reconnects automatically** (keep pressing Enter to retry on failure)
The first error line is now shown in the status bar when the first connection attempt fails
Fixed: unable to type after a successful connection (regression bug where the connection object was mistakenly deleted)
Fixed: duplicate session records — deduplicated by host+port+username, with historical duplicates cleaned up automatically at startup

**Critical fix**: the xterm library is now loaded from the app's own assets/ (the previous ../node_modules relative path broke inside the asar, causing "connection succeeded but the terminal UI failed to create, stuck on Connecting forever")
Added global script error display (red text in the UI) to eliminate silent failures
The UI shows the version number; the status bar ticks seconds live while connecting (30-second timeout cap)
readyTimeout shortened to 10 seconds

v1.4: fixed the authentication infinite-loop hang (custom authHandler retrying endlessly) by switching to the standard tryKeyboard + keyboard-interactive approach; added %TEMP%\easyssh-debug.log debug logging
v1.4.1: single-instance lock to prevent leftover processes causing "file in use" errors

Fixed the connection path that never resolved (added a close fallback and made done idempotent); keyboard-interactive authentication supported; a 30-second timeout fallback on the renderer side; the Linux-only cpu-features native module is excluded from packaging
electron-builder portable target: first **single-exe** output; sessions.json stored in the exe's real directory (PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_DIR)
First Windows x64 portable release (electron-packager folder build)
Project created: Electron + xterm.js + ssh2; multi-tab SSH, password/private key auth, 256-color terminal, window resize, keepalive, portable sessions
